observed_instead: The full gate on the release tree (version bumped to 0.3.9): py 5,127 passed and 26 skipped, ruff and all four mypy stages clean. The one failure is the documented contention flake src/app/tests/test_resident_transport.py::test_four_reader_runs_each_get_their_own_agent_process_at_once, which passes alone (re-run: 1 passed, exit 0); it failed the same way in earlier batch runs on the merged agent branches and passed alone each time, so it is environmental contention under parallel workers.

The site suite on the release tree: 41 of 41 passed, run twice end to end. A later repeat hit jsdom's HTMLCanvasElement.getContext race in the Turkish guide test; that test passes alone (2 passed) and no site file differs between the runs, so it is a jsdom/WebGL harness race, not a site failure.

One earlier release-tree run also failed test_dependencies_are_locked.py because the authoring-only [pipeline] extra installed into that venv had moved opentelemetry-api off its requirements.lock pin; restoring the pinned 1.45.1 makes the test pass, and the build venv installs requirements.lock itself.
Version agreement: pyproject.toml, kriko-ui/src-tauri/Cargo.toml, kriko-ui/src-tauri/Cargo.lock and kriko-ui/package.json all say 0.3.9, and the website's installer links name the 0.3.9 asset.
The extension keeps its 0.5.0 manifest and behaves the same; its panel and options CSS follow the app's neutral palette. The phone app (0.10.0) is unchanged and not part of this release.

Shared access keeps working across the upgrade: the build used the same stable pepper 0.3.8 shipped (copied into the clean worktree, not generated), so an access code handed out with 0.3.8 still opens in 0.3.9. The pepper is a build secret and is not in git.

The full build recipe (kriko-ui/package.ps1 -Version 0.3.9) completed on a clean requirements.lock venv (runtime closure + PyInstaller only): preflight versions agree; OpenSERP 0.8.12 verified; the frozen sidecar answered /api/health with version 0.3.9, extension 0.5.0 and no catalogs; web interface built; app and NSIS installer built; the built app stayed up 25 seconds and spawned its engine.

A separate frozen-sidecar harness re-checked handshake, /api/health (version 0.3.9, extension 0.5.0, no shell attached), API root, fresh store with no packs, extension, benchmark corpus, settings graphs, a lookup, a job and the MCP initialize: all passed, exit 0.

Artifacts: kriko-0.3.9-x86_64-setup.exe 33,092,141 bytes (31.6 MB); kriko-0.3.9-win64-portable.zip 42,397,156 bytes (40.4 MB); kriko-engine-0.3.9-win64.zip 27,772,400 bytes (26.5 MB); kriko-extension-0.5.0.zip 258,101 bytes; SHA256SUMS.txt.

Catalogs: 32 .kpack builds, packs.json whose rows are pinned to https://github.com/Berbadov/kriko/releases/download/v0.3.9, and packs-0.3.9.zip (33 entries, 2,401,697 bytes, sha256 4caa19029f3d231c2377ff6f7b993c2449657f93377313eaf38b2e0d9ab1d00d). Every index row, size and digest was checked against the built files before upload.

The shipped build used only requirements.lock and PyInstaller. An earlier attempt with the authoring [pipeline] extra installed froze the optional research tooling into a 30.7 MB engine; it was discarded and rebuilt on the locked closure (26.5 MB).
